Referred to the House Committee on Foreign Affairs.

dimensions.assessment: Affects federal agencies managing foreign assistance, implementing partners, and recipients of tangible U.S. foreign aid items.
dimensions.evidence: The United States flag shall be distinctively displayed on foreign assistance and... be the sole visual-branding element

dimensions.assessment: Imposes administrative and visual-branding rules on physical assets, food aid, medical supplies, and public outreach materials provided abroad.
dimensions.evidence: buildings, equipment, vehicles, project or construction site signage... food aid, medical supplies, and other commodities

dimensions.assessment: Requires rulemaking and branding updates by the Secretary of State, with no specific funding amounts stated.
dimensions.evidence: The Secretary of State shall issue such regulations as are necessary to implement this section

dimensions.assessment: Amends the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 by adding a new section regarding branding requirements and directed rulemaking.
dimensions.evidence: The Foreign Assistance Act of 1961 (22 U.S.C. 2151 et seq.) is amended

dimensions.assessment: Applies permanently to foreign assistance provided after the date of enactment.
dimensions.evidence: shall apply with respect to foreign assistance... provided after the date of the enactment of this Act.

missing_information: The administrative cost of redesigning or labeling foreign assistance items with the U.S. flag.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill mandates that the U.S. flag be distinctly displayed and be the sole visual-branding element on U.S. foreign assistance items, subject to specific exceptions and waivers.
